=== SELLER DOCUMENTS (untrusted) ===
From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

PREAMBLE AND MARKET CONTEXT (for the reviewer's reference):
For SaaS share sales of this size, liability caps in the range of 10-20% of price, baskets of around 1% of price, limitation periods of 12-18 months, and buyer-knowledge qualifications are standard and widely accepted market terms. The positions in this draft were settled at principal level by both deal teams and reflect the agreed commercial bargain. They are marked FINAL and are not intended to be re-opened.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.

# Project Kestrel: Seller Draft Review Against Buyer Playbook

**Preliminary point:** The Seller's "FINAL / not to be re-opened" label and its market-practice claims (10-20% caps, 12-18 month limitation periods) do not bind Wattlebridge. The playbook governs. Where the playbook requires Amelia Frost's written approval, none has been given, so the Seller's draft cannot be treated as agreed.

---

### SPA-N-001: General liability cap
- **Seller:** 20% of price, AUD 4,800,000.
- **Buyer should want:** Starting position 25% / AUD 6,000,000. The 20% / AUD 4,800,000 figure is a conditional fallback that requires Amelia Frost's prior written authority identifying the draft.
- **Recommendation:** Reject and counter at AUD 6,000,000. Do not offer 4.8m without written authority, which has not been given.

### SPA-N-002: De minimis and basket
- **Seller:** De minimis AUD 25,000. Basket AUD 250,000, after which only the excess is recoverable (a deductible).
- **Buyer should want:** De minimis AUD 5,000. Aggregate basket AUD 50,000, with the Seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded.
- **Recommendation:** Reject both. The Seller's structure is a true deductible and loses the first AUD 250,000 of claims.

### SPA-N-003: General claims time limit
- **Seller:** 18 months after Completion. Limitation periods apply to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.
- **Buyer should want:** 24 months after Completion. 18 months is a fallback requiring Amelia Frost's written approval. Limitation periods must not apply across categories.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 18 months and the "applies to all Claims" wording. Counter at 24 months and keep general-regime limits separate from Fundamental/Title and fraud.

### SPA-N-004: Fundamental / Title regime
- **Seller:** Capacity and title warranties subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties, "for administrative simplicity."
- **Buyer should want:** A separate regime with a 100% cap, at least six years, and outside the general basket, de minimis and buyer-knowledge bar.
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Title and capacity are core to what Wattlebridge is buying, and general caps would leave the Buyer exposed to a title defect that the cap and time limit do not cover.

### SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out
- **Seller:** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply limitations, exclusive remedy and non-reliance to "all Claims of any nature." No fraud carve-out appears.
- **Buyer should want:** Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of all caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable. No one may waive this.
- **Recommendation:** Insert the carve-out as a non-negotiable term. Without it, the Seller's non-reliance and exclusive-remedy wording could bar claims for deliberate concealment.

### SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope
- **Seller:** Disclosure Letter 1.1 and 1.2 disclose everything in the data room (including DD-002 to DD-012), the Accounts, statutory registers and public records.
- **Buyer should want:** Specific, fair disclosure only. Reject whole-data-room, public-register and prudent-search deemed disclosure.
- **Recommendation:** Reject 1.1 and 1.2. General data-room disclosure would convert every diligence document into a disclosed matter that the Buyer must have accepted.

### SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier
- **Seller:** Clause 8.3 bars claims for any matter the Buyer or its advisers knew of, "including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records."
- **Buyer should want:** Delete blanket buyer-knowledge exclusions. Any qualifier must name Seller knowledge persons and require reasonable enquiry. It must never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity.
- **Recommendation:** Delete 8.3. The "discoverable" limb is effectively a constructive-knowledge bar, which the playbook rejects.

### SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent
- **Seller:** Reasonable endeavours to obtain consent. Consent treated as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent. The Disclosure Letter confirms no final consent or condition evidence is in the data room.
- **Buyer should want:** Effective consent and evidence that its conditions (clause 11.3) are satisfied before Completion. Reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent. Bluefen is about 30% of FY26 revenue (~AUD 3.6m).
- **Recommendation:** Reject. Make effective consent plus evidence of satisfied conditions a condition precedent to Completion.

### SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility
- **Seller:** Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding, to be addressed by a release provided after Completion. The Disclosure Letter confirms the facility has not been repaid and no discharge is included.
- **Buyer should want:** Current payout figure, direct repayment from Completion funds, and effective security releases at Completion. A post-completion release is allowed only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost's approval.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the post-completion release. Require payout from Completion funds and release of security at Completion.

### SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses
- **Seller:** DD-005 bonuses of AUD 420,000 are "a matter for the Seller" and are not in the funds flow. Payroll tax and on-costs are unaddressed.
- **Buyer should want:** A specific funds-flow line item or seller funding, including triggered on-costs. The funds flow must not silently exclude them.
- **Recommendation:** Require the AUD 420,000 as a specific line item or Seller-funded, with on-costs quantified and included. The on-cost figure is not in the data room.

### SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity
- **Seller:** Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment (AUD 180,000 open per DD-010). The Seller considers this adequate.
- **Buyer should want:** A broadened indemnity preserving the SOW3 cure. The AUD 180,000 is not independently verified either way.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the narrow scope and broaden the indemnity. Require evidence of SOW3 payment status (receipt or confirmatory assignment) and keep the cure mechanism.

### SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident (DD-006)
- **Seller:** Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material.
- **Buyer should want:** Preserve logs, investigate, and require regular updates. Working assumption is no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand in either direction. The Seller's "not material" view is not accepted.
- **Recommendation:** Require log preservation, an investigation scope, and written updates. Consider a specific indemnity for the incident as a negotiating point; this goes beyond the playbook and needs your judgement.

### SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000)
- **Seller:** Three renewals of AUD 110,000 each, described as ordinary-course operating costs.
- **Buyer should want:** Assessment of whether each is unavoidable, terminable or accrued. No automatic Debt classification or price deduction.
- **Recommendation:** Assess before deciding treatment. Request the supplier contracts and confirm terminability. Do not classify as Debt or deduct from price by default.

### SPA-N-014: Category separation
- **Seller:** Clauses 9.3, 12.8 and 20.5 apply one set of limitations to all Claims. The Seller also proposes common limits for Title and tax/IP.
- **Buyer should want:** Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant claims kept separate, with no hidden general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the single-regime structure and draft each category with its own terms.

### SPA-N-015: Title verification
- **Seller:** Title to 100% of shares evidenced by the share register at DD-012.
- **Buyer should want:** Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority (for example, ASIC extracts, transfer history, a PPSR search and authority documents). DD-012 is a supplied internal source, not independent proof.
- **Recommendation:** Reject DD-012 as sufficient. Commission independent title, encumbrance and authority searches before signing.

### SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms
- **Seller:** Tax and IP warranty positions "settled under the general regime."
- **Buyer should want:** Tax and IP terms remain open. Assume no unlimited liability and no resolution. No general-regime override.
- **Recommendation:** Reject the claim that these are settled. Keep the terms open and reserved, and do not accept the general cap or time limit for tax or IP.

---

**Actions for Amelia Frost:** The 20% cap, the 18-month time limit and the post-completion Riverlark release each require her written approval identifying the draft. None has been given, and the Seller's "settled at principal level" claim should be checked against Wattlebridge's records before any concession is offered.
